sections.h2: Which selling paths suit a Horizon City owner?
sections.html:
Use a broker, sell privately, or take cash. Owners live in 85.2% of Horizon City homes per the Census Bureau, so the typical seller is a family leaving a house they have lived in.

Choose a cash proposal when you need a firm closing day or would rather not pay for repairs. Choose a listing when the house is in good order and you can wait for a buyer who needs financing. Whichever you pick, do the same prep first.

  • Collect the deed, your latest tax statement and any utility district bills.
  • Ask each buyer for terms in writing: price, closing day and who pays what.
  • Ask for proof of funds before you stop showing the house.

sections.h2: Where is Horizon City and how was it built?
sections.html:
The town's comprehensive plan places Horizon City on the Hueco Bolson about 15 miles east of El Paso, with the Franklin Mountains to the west and Mexico roughly 20 miles south. It lists an elevation of 4,022 feet, around 7.77 inches of rain a year, and a July average high of 94 degrees Fahrenheit.

According to that plan, a Chicago-based developer announced the project in December 1959, and a planning outfit from Tucson laid the town out beside the proposed Interstate 10 route. The first house sold on October 31, 1962, and by 1971 only about 94 homes were occupied. Horizon City incorporated on August 13, 1988, and voters adopted a charter in November 1997. It is a home rule city with a mayor and seven council members.

Desert sun and dry air are tough on roofs, stucco and paint, and inspectors check cooling equipment closely. Handle cheap repairs before showing the house, or price in the ones you leave.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Horizon City homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists a median home value of $170,200 for 2020 to 2024 and 25,118 residents in 2025, which is 11.8% above the 2020 base of 22,461. Steady growth keeps new subdivisions coming, so your house competes with new construction.

Households average 3.39 people, so buyers often want extra bedrooms. The 29.4-minute average commute points to workers heading into El Paso, which makes access to Interstate 10 and Eastlake Boulevard part of what you are selling.

sections.h2: Who is buying in Horizon City, and what do they want?
sections.html:
Horizon City skews young. QuickFacts reports 33.7% of residents under 18 and only 5.5% age 65 or older, and 92.5% of people lived in the same house a year earlier, which is a stable base of families. Larger households tend to look for extra bedrooms, a yard and an easy run to Interstate 10.

Language is part of the picture too: 73.5% of residents speak a language other than English at home and 23.2% are foreign-born. If a family member who reads Spanish will help you with the sale, ask the buyer to give you the contract and disclosures in a form you can read before you sign.

Median household income is $65,737, and the poverty rate is 22.0%. A clean, working house with a documented repair history will draw more interest than one with open questions.

sections.h2: Does the town have rules for building and land use?
sections.html:
Yes. The comprehensive plan says development activity falls under the Planning and Zoning Commission and the Board of Adjustment, which make recommendations to the council on zoning and related matters. If you added a room, fence, carport or pool, ask town hall whether it was permitted, because lenders and title companies sometimes ask.

The plan also notes that the town has about 5.7 square miles within its limits as of 2011, while QuickFacts counts 8.71 square miles of land in 2020, so ask the town for the current boundary. If your lot is near the edge, confirm whether it sits inside the town or in the county, since that decides who issues permits and provides services.

The same plan suggests studying bike routes, sidewalks and street lighting on principal streets such as Darrington Road and Eastlake Boulevard. Buyers who care about traffic and walkability may ask about plans for the street your house faces.

sections.h2: Which schools and offices matter to a Horizon City seller?
sections.html:
The plan names the Socorro and Clint school districts and the Horizon Regional Municipal Utility District among local agencies. Buyers ask which district serves a home, so confirm it on your tax bill.

The El Paso Central Appraisal District values all real and business personal property in El Paso County. Its home page links to protests and appeals, exemption forms, a deadline calendar and a taxpayer liaison who helps with complaints about the review board. Check that calendar for the protest date that applies to you.

  • Appraisal district: your value and exemptions.
  • County tax office: the bill and a payoff statement.
  • County clerk: deed and other recorded papers.
  • Town hall: permits, zoning and utility accounts.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded in El Paso County and what does it cost?
sections.html:
The El Paso County Clerk records deeds. An instrument conveying land can be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer, or sworn before two witnesses.

The 2023 clerk manual published by Texas Courts lists $5.00 for page one, $4.00 for each added page and $0.25 for every name beyond five that must be indexed. It also lists records fees, such as $2.00 for technology and up to $10 each for management and archive. A missing grantee address can add $25. Counties can change these figures, so ask the clerk for the current schedule.

A title company normally files the deed for you. It goes to the county where the land sits, so a Horizon City house is recorded in El Paso County. The manual says nothing of a transfer tax, so ask your title company for a settlement statement showing every charge.

sections.h2: What does an unpaid tax bill mean for a sale?
sections.html:
The lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1 and follows the property, not the owner. The Comptroller says a court can order a foreclosure sale even after ownership changes, and a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid.

Taxes are delinquent after January 31, and penalty and interest begin on February 1. If a house sells at a tax sale, a Texas Supreme Court opinion describes redemption: homestead, farm and mineral property can be redeemed within two years after the purchaser's deed is filed, at a 25 percent premium in year one and 50 percent in year two, and other property within 180 days. The State Law Library adds that a former owner has two years to claim surplus from a tax foreclosure sale.

If you are behind, selling before a suit saves court costs. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure and whether it offers an installment plan, which some collectors allow for a residence homestead.

faqs.q: How many people live in Horizon City?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 25,118 on July 1, 2025, which is 11.8% above the April 2020 base.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: The county clerk manual lists recording fees and says nothing of a transfer tax. Ask your title company for the full settlement statement.

faqs.q: Can I sell with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes, if the balance is paid at or before closing, since the lien follows the house. Request a payoff statement from the county tax office.

faqs.q: Who decides the value of my property for tax?
faqs.a: The El Paso Central Appraisal District. Use its calendar for protest dates and its taxpayer liaison if you have a complaint.

faqs.q: Is $170,200 the price my house will fetch?
faqs.a: That is the Census median for owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024 across the whole town. Ask for written offers or an appraisal for your own address.
